$comment: Online sources shipped with GoTek Manager. Edit this file rather than the code.
It is bundled at build time, and overridden at run time by a providers.json placed
in the application's configuration folder, whose path is shown in Settings. An
override replaces this list entirely; entries that fail validation are dropped and
Fields: id (unique), name, adapter (internetArchive | htmlSite | jsonFeed),
platformId (omit for every platform), query (search adapters), catalogUrl (site and
feed adapters), note (shown in the interface), ignoreRobots, userAgent.
Every URL below was checked for reachability and against the site's robots.txt,
reading the wildcard group the way a crawler does. What none of that can tell you
is whether a crawl finds anything: website inspection follows same-site pages two
levels deep and records links ending in a format this platform uses, which suits a
file index and does not suit a database whose downloads sit behind a script. Sites
of the second kind are included because they are where the software is, and are
marked as such. Refresh one to find out what it yields.
A GoTek presents floppy images. New software for the 8-bit Commodores is almost
always .d64, which is a 1541 GCR recording a GoTek cannot reproduce, so those
sources will mostly show titles that cannot be used until someone converts them.

providers.name: Internet Archive
providers.note: Searches any machine by name. The one source that applies whatever you are preparing.

providers.name: Stairway to Hell: BBC
providers.note: A file index, which is the shape this adapter handles best.

providers.name: 8-Bit Software
providers.note: The 8BS archive, still publishing new BBC material. Downloads are ZIP archives, which are unpacked automatically.

providers.name: Stardot
providers.note: Where most new BBC and Electron software is announced. A forum, so expect attachments rather than a tidy index.

providers.name: BBC Micro Games Archive
providers.note: By far the richest BBC source found: thirty-six .ssd links on its front page alone. Its robots.txt refuses automated clients, so it does nothing until you enable the override on this source and accept what that means.

providers.name: Stairway to Hell: Electron
providers.note: A file index, which is the shape this adapter handles best.

providers.name: Acorn Electron World
providers.note: Long-running Electron archive, including recent releases. Publishes no robots.txt.

providers.name: 8-Bit Software
providers.note: Covers the Electron alongside the BBC.

providers.name: Internet Archive: Amstrad CPC
providers.note: 3,809 items.

providers.name: CPCRulez
providers.note: Active CPC community with new releases and type-ins. Database-driven, so a crawl may find less than the site holds.

providers.name: CPC-POWER
providers.note: The largest CPC catalogue, new releases included. Database-driven. Publishes no robots.txt.

providers.name: Internet Archive: Amstrad CPC
providers.note: 3,809 items.

providers.name: CPCRulez
providers.note: Active CPC community with new releases and type-ins.

providers.name: CPC-POWER
providers.note: The largest CPC catalogue, new releases included.

providers.name: Internet Archive: Commodore 64
providers.note: 98,846 items, of which a sample is fetched.

providers.name: CSDb
providers.note: Where the C64 scene publishes new demos and games first. Most releases are .d64, which a GoTek cannot present; only .d81 and .hfe are usable.

providers.name: RGCD
providers.note: Publishes new commercial C64 games. Small catalogue, cartridge and disk.

providers.name: Protovision
providers.note: New commercial C64 titles. A shop, so most links lead to a purchase rather than a download.

providers.name: Internet Archive: Commodore 128
providers.note: No collection of its own; a subject search returning tens of items.

providers.name: CSDb
providers.note: Covers the 128 alongside the 64. The 1581 is the drive a GoTek can stand in for, so look for .d81.

providers.name: Protovision
providers.note: Occasionally publishes 128-compatible titles.

providers.name: Internet Archive: Commodore Plus/4
providers.query: mediatype:software AND (subject:"plus/4" OR title:"Plus/4" OR subject:"commodore plus4")
providers.note: No collection of its own; a subject search returning tens of items.

providers.name: Plus/4 World
providers.note: The Plus/4 archive, and where new Plus/4 software appears. Database-driven.

providers.name: CSDb
providers.note: Carries Plus/4 releases among the Commodore scene output.

providers.name: Internet Archive: Amiga
providers.note: 13,207 items.

providers.name: Aminet
providers.note: Still the largest Amiga archive and still receiving new uploads. Most files are .lha rather than .adf, so a crawl finds fewer usable images than the size of the archive suggests.

providers.name: English Amiga Board
providers.note: Where new Amiga work is announced and shared. A forum, so expect attachments.

providers.name: Internet Archive: ZX Spectrum
providers.note: 12,305 items.

providers.name: ZX-Art
providers.note: Catalogues new Spectrum releases as they appear. Much of it is tape, which a GoTek cannot present; look for .trd and .mgt.

providers.name: World of Spectrum
providers.note: The long-standing Spectrum archive, now including modern releases.

providers.name: Internet Archive: ZX Spectrum
providers.note: 12,305 items. A 48K title runs on a 128K.

providers.name: ZX-Art
providers.note: New Spectrum releases. The +3 uses .dsk, which this platform accepts.

providers.name: World of Spectrum
providers.note: The long-standing Spectrum archive, now including modern releases.

providers.name: ZX Spectrum Next
providers.note: The official site, which carries the system distribution and links to new software.

providers.name: itch.io: ZX Spectrum
providers.note: Where most new Next software is published. itch.io permits crawling but refuses its own download endpoints, so this finds pages rather than files, and much of what it lists is paid. Buy it there.

providers.name: Internet Archive: Atari ST
providers.note: 884 items.

providers.name: Atarimania
providers.note: The most complete ST catalogue. Database-driven: a two-level crawl of its listings found no direct images, so treat this as a place to look rather than a source that fills a stick.

providers.name: Demozoo: Atari ST
providers.note: New ST demos and intros, actively curated. Downloads are hosted elsewhere, so results vary.

providers.name: Internet Archive: Atari 8-bit
providers.note: 4,729 items.

providers.name: ABBUC
providers.note: Runs the annual software competition that produces most new Atari 8-bit games. Publishes no robots.txt.

providers.name: AtariAge
providers.note: The main homebrew community for Atari hardware. A forum and a shop, so expect links to purchases as well as downloads.
